<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Synthetic\Accessors\Formats;

use Synthetic\Accessors\Accessor;

/** Reads `KEY=value` lines. Blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; a value may be wrapped in one pair of matching quotes. */
final class EnvAccessor implements Accessor
{
    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private array $values = [];

    public function __construct(string $source)
    {
        foreach (preg_split('/\r?\n/', $source) ?: [] as $raw) {
            $line = trim($raw);
            if ($line === '' || str_starts_with($line, '#')) {
                continue;
            }
            $eq = strpos($line, '=');
            if ($eq === false || $eq === 0) {
                continue;
            }
            $key = trim(substr($line, 0, $eq));
            $value = trim(substr($line, $eq + 1));
            if (strlen($value) >= 2 && ($value[0] === '"' || $value[0] === "'") && $value[strlen($value) - 1] === $value[0]) {
                $value = substr($value, 1, -1);
            }
            $this->values[$key] = $value;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $key, ?string $fallback = null): ?string
    {
        return $this->values[$key] ?? $fallback;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return array_key_exists($key, $this->values);
    }

    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->values;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__ . '/../src/Accessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/EnvAccessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/JsonAccessor.php';

use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\EnvAccessor;
use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\JsonAccessor;

$failures = 0;
function check(string $name, bool $ok): void
{
    global $failures;
    echo ($ok ? "ok   " : "FAIL ") . $name . "\n";
    if (!$ok) {
        $failures++;
    }
}

$env = new EnvAccessor("HOST=localhost\nPORT=3000\n");
check('reads KEY=value lines', $env->get('HOST') === 'localhost' && $env->get('PORT') === '3000');

$env = new EnvAccessor("# a comment\n\nKEY=value\n");
check('skips blank lines and comments', $env->all() === ['KEY' => 'value']);

$env = new EnvAccessor("A=\"one two\"\nB='three'\n");
check('strips one pair of matching quotes', $env->get('A') === 'one two' && $env->get('B') === 'three');

$env = new EnvAccessor('KEY=value');
check('answers the fallback for a key that is not there', $env->get('MISSING', 'none') === 'none' && $env->has('KEY') && !$env->has('MISSING'));

$json = new JsonAccessor('{"name":"x","count":3}');
check('json keeps the string values of an object', $json->all() === ['name' => 'x']);

exit($failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Synthetic\Accessors\Formats;

use Synthetic\Accessors\Accessor;

/** Reads `KEY=value` lines. Blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; a value may be wrapped in one pair of matching quotes. */
final class EnvAccessor implements Accessor
{
    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private array $values = [];

    public function __construct(string $source)
    {
        foreach (preg_split('/\r?\n/', $source) ?: [] as $raw) {
            $line = trim($raw);
            if ($line === '' || str_starts_with($line, '#')) {
                continue;
            }
            $eq = strpos($line, '=');
            if ($eq === false || $eq === 0) {
                continue;
            }
            $key = trim(substr($line, 0, $eq));
            $value = trim(substr($line, $eq + 1));
            if (strlen($value) >= 2 && ($value[0] === '"' || $value[0] === "'") && $value[strlen($value) - 1] === $value[0]) {
                $value = substr($value, 1, -1);
            }
            $this->values[$key] = $value;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $key, ?string $fallback = null): ?string
    {
        return $this->values[$key] ?? $fallback;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return array_key_exists($key, $this->values);
    }

    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->values;
    }
}

input.title: EnvAccessor drops a leading `export` only when it is a keyword, not a key
input.rationale: Lines written `export KEY=value` (a shell habit) are read as `KEY=value`. The prefix is stripped with `^export[ \t]+(?=[^ \t=])` after the line is trimmed, in both the JS and the PHP EnvAccessor (ADR-1: a behavior change is made in both packages in the same pull request). The pattern is the same in both and spells out space and tab rather than `\s`, because JS `\s` matches Unicode whitespace and PCRE without /u does not, which would make the two packages disagree on exotic whitespace. The lookahead means `export` is a keyword only when a key follows it: `export=1`, `export_path=2`, `exported=3` and `export =4` still read as keys named `export`, `export_path`, `exported` and `export`, as they did before. `export HOST` with no `=` is skipped like any other line without one, and a commented-out `# export KEY=value` stays a comment.
input.alternatives: Strip a bare `export ` prefix with startsWith/str_starts_with: rejected, it would turn `export =4` into a line starting with `=` and silently drop a key that used to parse, and it handles only one space. Use `\s+` in the pattern: rejected, JS and PHP disagree on what `\s` matches, so the two packages could read the same line differently. Strip `export` anywhere in the key: rejected, `exported=3` and `export_path=2` are ordinary keys.

content.text:
`EnvAccessor` now reads `export KEY=value` as `KEY=value`, and I made the same change in the PHP package, which you didn't ask for. Both suites pass: 9 of 9 in JS and every check in PHP.

**PHP port.** This repo's accepted decision ADR-1 says a behavior change in one package is made in the other in the same pull request. It governs `packages/js/src` and `packages/php/src`, so I ported the change to `packages/php/src/Formats/EnvAccessor.php`. If you'd rather keep this JS-only, revert the two PHP files, but that goes against ADR-1.

**The change.** After trimming, each line has a leading `export` plus spaces or tabs removed, but only when a key follows. The pattern is `^export[ \t]+(?=[^ \t=])` in both languages. I wrote space and tab out instead of using `\s`, because JS and PCRE disagree on which characters `\s` matches.

**What stays as it was:**
- `export=1`, `export_path=2`, `exported=3` and `export =4` are still ordinary keys.
- `export HOST` with no `=` is skipped.
- `# export KEY=value` is still a comment.

**Tests.** I added three tests in `packages/js/tests/env-accessor.test.ts` and the same three checks in `packages/php/tests/run.php`:
- the basic form, with a double space, a tab and quoted values
- keys that only start with `export`
- an export with no value, a commented-out export, and an indented one

**Record.** I recorded ADR-2 for the "keyword, not key" rule, with the alternatives I turned down. It is still `proposed` and waits for someone to accept it. ADR-1 also lists a `parity-vectors.json` and a `composer test:parity` check. There is no vectors file in this repo, and the `test:parity` scripts just run the ordinary tests, so no shared vectors needed updating.

I haven't committed anything. When you commit, include the new files under `.mnema/` (ADR-2 and this session's key and tail) with the code.
